suggestedPlan.title: ONE SUGGESTED PLAN. ZERO GROUP MATH.
suggestedPlan.body: Balances reconcile to the cent, then Split suggests a short list of who should pay whom. Pay however your group already pays.

step1.body: Name it and pick a currency — Split draws it for you. Ski trip, flat bills, Tuesday dinner.

step3.body: Balances update live, and the maths reconciles to the cent.

item2.title: Flatmates

item4.title: Remote crews

item1.title: Free forever

item2.title: No account needed

footer.tagline: Split any bill with a link. Peanut Split is made by the team behind Peanut.

install.title: Add Split to your home screen
install.body: Opens instantly, works like an app. No store, no account.

ios.title: Add Split to your home screen
ios.step1: Tap the Share button in the Safari toolbar.
ios.step2: Scroll down and choose “Add to Home Screen”.
ios.body: Two taps in Safari and Split lives on your home screen like an app.

bearer.title: The link is the key
bearer.body: There are no accounts, so there is nothing to log into. Anyone holding the link can open the room and add expenses — keep it in the group chat and it stays with the group.

private.title: Nobody finds it by accident
private.body: Room pages are kept out of search engines and the address ends in a random tail, so it cannot be guessed. It only reaches the people you send it to.

lost.title: If everyone loses it, the room is gone
lost.body: Rooms you have opened are listed on this page, saved on your device. That is the trade for not asking anyone to make an account.

nothingElse.title: Split never touches your money
nothingElse.body: It records who paid what and who owes whom. The payments themselves happen wherever you already make them.

readMore.toggleHint: Who made it, why it is free, and the awkward questions.

join.title: What your friends see
join.body: One tap and a name. No email, no password, nothing to download — what you are asking of them is smaller than what you are asking of yourself.

currency.title: 12 supported currencies
currency.body: The room counts in one currency. Add an expense in any of the 12 supported currencies and Split converts it at the rate on the day.

splits.title: Splits that are not even
splits.body: Equal, by shares, by exact amounts, or with some people left out of a line.

exact.title: Reconciles to the cent
exact.body: Balances always sum to zero, and you can open any balance to see exactly how it was reached.

live.title: Everyone sees it at once
live.body: Add something on the bus and it is on everyone else’s screen before you get off.

offline.title: Works with no signal
offline.body: Type an expense in a basement or up a mountain. It waits on your phone and goes when the signal comes back.

home.title: Add it to your home screen

transfers.title: A simpler payment plan
transfers.body: Split turns a web of balances into a short suggested list of who should pay whom.

settle.title: How you get paid back
settle.body: Split tells you who should pay whom. You send the money the way you already would, and the room records that you did.

team.title: The people who built it
team.intro: Split has no users yet, so there is nobody to quote but us.

konrad.name: Konrad
konrad.quote: Every trip ended the same way: a spreadsheet nobody updated, and one person quietly out of pocket.

hugo.name: Hugo
hugo.quote: I wanted the whole thing to be a link. If your friends have to make an account, they will not.

who.title: Who made this, and why it is free

built.title: Peanut built Split
built.body: Peanut is a payments app and a real company with a real product — not a weekend project that disappears.

free.title: It is free because it introduces people to Peanut
free.body: No premium tier, no upsell coming, nothing to buy.

data.title: There is not much here to leak
data.body: Room links are kept out of our own analytics, because a link is a key.

retype.q: Do I have to retype everything from the group chat?
retype.a: For a trip that already happened, yes — the expenses get typed in once. It is lighter than it sounds, because everyone in the room can add their own instead of it all landing on you.
retype.import: If you are coming from Splitwise, the import page brings a whole group across in one step.

access.a: Anyone with the link. It is kept out of search engines and cannot be guessed, but it is a key — keep it in the group chat rather than anywhere public.

lost.q: What happens if we lose the link?
lost.a: Rooms you have opened are saved on your device and listed on the home page. If nobody in the group still has it, the room is gone.

limits.q: Is there a limit on how many expenses we can add?
limits.a: No. Add fifty in an afternoon if that is the kind of trip it is.

warnings.title: Worth knowing
warnings.ROW_UNBALANCED: Row {row} does not add up in the file itself, so it was left out.
warnings.ROW_UNSUPPORTED_CURRENCY: Row {row} is in {detail}, which Split does not carry yet, so it was left out.
warnings.ROW_NO_PAYER: Row {row} does not say who paid, so it was left out.
warnings.ROW_ZERO_COST: Row {row} has no amount, so it was left out.
warnings.ROW_BAD_AMOUNT: Row {row} has an amount we could not read, so it was left out.
warnings.ROW_BAD_DATE: Row {row} has a date we could not read — it comes in dated today.
warnings.ROW_DESCRIPTION_TRUNCATED: Row {row} has a very long description — it comes in shortened.
warnings.ROW_CATEGORY_TRUNCATED: Row {row} has a very long category — it comes in shortened.
warnings.MEMBER_NAME_TRUNCATED: One name was too long and comes in shortened, as “{detail}”. You can edit it above.
warnings.MULTI_PAYER_SPLIT: “{detail}” was paid by more than one person. The file does not record who put in what, so it arrives as one expense per payer — the balances are exact, the split between payers is our best reading.
warnings.PAYMENT_ROWS: Payments between people arrive as expenses rather than as settled-up records. The balances come out the same.
warnings.DUPLICATE_MEMBER_NAME: Two people are called {detail}, so the second is listed as “{detail} (2)”. Rename them below.
warnings.TRUNCATED_HISTORY: A room holds 500 expenses, so the {count, plural, one {# oldest one} other {# oldest ones}} arrive as a single “Balance brought forward” entry per person instead. Everyone's balance still comes out the same.

errors.NOT_SPLITWISE_CSV: That does not look like a Splitwise export. It should be the .csv you get from “Export as spreadsheet”.
errors.NO_MEMBERS: That export has no people in it — check you exported a group rather than a single expense.
errors.NO_EXPENSES: There was nothing we could read in that file. If its expenses are in a currency Split does not carry, that would be why.
errors.TOO_MANY_MEMBERS: That group has more than 20 people. Split rooms are built for a trip or a flat, not a mailing list.
errors.TOO_MANY_EXPENSES: That export has more than 500 expenses. Try a group with less history, or start a fresh room.
errors.FILE_TOO_BIG: That file is too big to be a Splitwise export. Check you picked the right one.
errors.READ_FAILED: We could not read that file. Try choosing it again.
errors.DUPLICATE_NAMES: Two people have the same name — make them different so every expense lands on the right person.
